currentContext.strengths: World's largest thermal lamination film producer and second-largest specialty label film producer globally; among top four global players in BOPP specialty films|Widest product portfolio under one roof combined with customised innovation, allocation flexibility across job lines, scale, global reach and global warehousing facility|R&D-led moat: advanced R&D centre in Aurangabad, 30+ researchers including PhDs and post-doctoral professionals, six registered patents with eleven more in pipeline (seven India, four overseas)|De-commoditising product mix: speciality films accounted for 59% of FY26 sales|Global distribution reach: exports to 100+ countries, ~44% of sales from exports, office presence in 7 countries
currentContext.strategies: Growth anchored in specialisation across five verticals with distinct identities under one roof — Cosmo Films (flexible packaging), Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging), Cosmo Speciality Chemicals, Cosmo Consumer (window films/PPF), and Zigly (pet care) — sharing a common foundation of innovation and customer focus|Continue to de-commoditise the flagship film business by increasing focus on speciality films and sustained R&D investment, particularly on sustainability, to drive long-term sustainable growth|Maximise returns from the ₹1,200 crore strategic capital investments undertaken over the last three years, with each business vertical targeted on enhancing intrinsic value through disciplined emphasis on high-margin opportunities and superior ROCE|Strengthen financial resilience by reducing corporate net debt substantially over the next 2 years|Expand global footprint through international partnerships and operations — 50:50 joint venture with Filmax Corporation (South Korea) and expanded North American finishing operations at Carol Stream, Illinois|Advance toward a sustainable, green future by developing films from mono-material structures that are easily recyclable, helping customers reduce their carbon footprint|In Speciality Chemicals, focus each of the three verticals (coating chemicals, masterbatch, adhesives) on niche specialties addressing current industry problem areas or offering significantly superior products versus what is currently available|In Cosmo Plastech, focus on establishing direct-to-brand partnerships with leading FMCG companies rather than intermediated sales
currentContext.expansion: Cosmo First has invested Rs 1,180 crore over the last three years in multiple growth projects spanning BOPP, CPP & Polyester lines, Metallizers, Coating lines, Window/PPF films, Zigly and Rigid Packaging. During the year the Company commissioned a state-of-the-art 10.4-meter, 5-layer BOPP film line with annual capacity of 81.2 KMT (one of the highest-capacity lines globally), taking total BOPP capacity to approximately 277 KMT per annum across 10 lines, up from 196 KMT (9 lines) a year earlier. Coated Specialty Films capacity was similarly expanded to 45,000 MT (10 lines) from 36,000 MT (8 lines). The Company also strengthened its global footprint via a 50:50 joint venture with Filmax Corporation (Korea) for marketing and distribution of flexible packaging products, launched the Cosmo Consumer vertical (Cosmo Sunshield window films, now in 100+ Indian cities/towns, and Cosmo PPF paint protection films), and grew Zigly's pet-care experience-centre network to over 40 stores as of March 2026, including the acquisition of two veterinary hospitals (Mumbai and Bengaluru). Cosmo First holds six registered patents with eleven more in the pipeline (seven in India, four overseas).

growth verticals / optionality: Zigly spin-off/external funding planned FY27; US/Europe expansion for Auto Care films (currently <20% util); Specialty Chemicals volume growth (20% YoY) masked by lower RM prices; Tariff refund >INR 60 Cr expected over 6-12 months.
margins & cost dynamics: BOPP/BOPET spreads volatile but Q4 strong (BOPP INR 20/kg, BOPET INR 18/kg); Specialty lag in price pass-through (1-3 months) caused slight Q4 dip; Employee costs up 30% YoY due to scaling, expected to stabilize at Q4 run-rate + inflation; New businesses (Plastech/Consumer) dragging PBT due to marketing spend despite EBITDA breakeven.
capex / expansion: Strategic CAPEX cycle complete (INR 1,200 Cr spent over 3 years); FY27 guidance <INR 100 Cr for maintenance/minor expansion; Focus on sweating assets.
capital allocation: Debt reduction priority (target <2x EBITDA in 12-18 months); Dividend INR 4/share recommended; Exploring external capital for Zigly to fund growth without balance sheet strain.

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.

hero.oneLiner: World's largest producer of thermal lamination films and second-largest producer of specialty label films globally, and a leading player in the Indian BOPP films market, diversifying into specialty chemicals, rigid packaging, window/paint-protection films and pet care.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: World's largest producer of thermal lamination films and second-largest producer of specialty label films globally, and a leading player in the Indian BOPP films market, diversifying into specialty chemicals, rigid packaging, window/paint-protection films and pet care.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Cosmo First (formerly Cosmo Films, est. 1981) manufactures BOPP, BOPET, thermal lamination, coated specialty, metalised and CPP flexible packaging films for FMCG brands, flexible packaging converters, label manufacturers and channel partners in India and 100+ export countries. The Company has diversified beyond films into specialty chemicals (coating chemicals, masterbatch, adhesives) under Cosmo Speciality Chemicals, end-to-end rigid packaging under Cosmo Plastech, window films/paint protection films under the Cosmo Consumer division (Cosmo Sunshield, Cosmo PPF, Cosmo Guard), and a direct-to-consumer pet care vertical under the Zigly brand.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Films: Q4 Sales vol +41%, BOPP margin INR 20/kg, BOPET INR 18/kg, Specialty mix 60% (targeting 70% in 18-24mo). Specialty Chemicals: Q4 Sales INR 54 Cr, EBITDA margin >25%; FY26 Sales INR 204 Cr. Rigid Packaging (Plastech): Q4 Sales +70% YoY, reached EBITDA breakeven. Consumer (Zigly + Auto): Zigly Q4 +54% YoY (annualized run rate INR 90 Cr); Auto Care Q4 exit rate INR 38 Cr (FY26 total INR 23 Cr), gross margin 35-40%.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Flexible Packaging Films:** BOPP films, BOPET films, Thermal lamination films, Coated specialty films, Metalised films, CPP films, CSP films, High barrier films, Velvet thermal lamination films, Direct thermal printable films
- **Speciality Chemicals:** Coating chemicals, Masterbatches, Adhesives
- **Rigid Packaging (Cosmo Plastech):** Injection-moulded rigid packaging, Thermoformed rigid packaging
- **Cosmo Consumer:** Cosmo Sunshield (window films), Cosmo PPF (paint protection film), Cosmo Guard (surface protection)
- **Pet Care:** Zigly D2C omni-channel stores, Zigly Lifestyle, Applod, Furpro, Veterinary hospitals (Mumbai, Bengaluru)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A (Make-to-order model); Management highlights 15-20% volume growth potential from existing installed capacity in Films; Specialty Chemicals has INR 100 Cr volume upside; Plastech has 30% volume upside.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue: Double-digit growth FY27 driven by unutilized capacity; Margin: BOPP/BOPET volatile but Specialty mix improving; US operations to benefit from tariff removal; Capex: <INR 100 Cr FY27 (cycle complete).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Zigly spin-off/external funding planned FY27; US/Europe expansion for Auto Care films (currently <20% util); Specialty Chemicals volume growth (20% YoY) masked by lower RM prices; Tariff refund >INR 60 Cr expected over 6-12 months.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic demand and supply scenario for flexible packaging is expected to remain favourable in the coming years, aided by e-commerce growth, food & beverage demand, sustainability/recyclability trends, and urbanisation
- Speciality chemicals demand supported by rapid urbanisation, government infrastructure programmes (e.g. Smart Cities Mission), rising middle-class disposable incomes, EV adhesive demand and renewable energy installations
- Rigid packaging growth driven by rising demand for packaged goods and beverages and by deeper direct engagement with leading FMCG brand customers
- Window/sun-control film segment: with only two domestic manufacturers of window films in India, management views this as a significant high-margin growth opportunity; demand also driven by rising awareness of energy efficiency and sustainable building materials
- Pet care segment demand supported by premiumisation and the largely non-discretionary, resilient nature of pet-related spending, alongside rising pet ownership in India
- Speciality films sales mix reached 59% of FY26 sales, reflecting a continuing shift away from commodity films toward higher-margin speciality products
- FY26 consolidated EBITDA improvement attributed to higher volumes following commissioning of new BOPP and CPP lines, growth in speciality films, and improved profitability in the specialty chemicals business
- BOPET line specialty product pipeline: company is introducing new specialty products including window films, security films, PET-G films, and others

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: BOPP/BOPET spreads volatile but Q4 strong (BOPP INR 20/kg, BOPET INR 18/kg); Specialty lag in price pass-through (1-3 months) caused slight Q4 dip; Employee costs up 30% YoY due to scaling, expected to stabilize at Q4 run-rate + inflation; New businesses (Plastech/Consumer) dragging PBT due to marketing spend despite EBITDA breakeven.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt reduction priority (target <2x EBITDA in 12-18 months); Dividend INR 4/share recommended; Exploring external capital for Zigly to fund growth without balance sheet strain.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Cosmo First has invested Rs 1,180 crore over the last three years in multiple growth projects spanning BOPP, CPP & Polyester lines, Metallizers, Coating lines, Window/PPF films, Zigly and Rigid Packaging. During the year the Company commissioned a state-of-the-art 10.4-meter, 5-layer BOPP film line with annual capacity of 81.2 KMT (one of the highest-capacity lines globally), taking total BOPP capacity to approximately 277 KMT per annum across 10 lines, up from 196 KMT (9 lines) a year earlier. Coated Specialty Films capacity was similarly expanded to 45,000 MT (10 lines) from 36,000 MT (8 lines). The Company also strengthened its global footprint via a 50:50 joint venture with Filmax Corporation (Korea) for marketing and distribution of flexible packaging products, launched the Cosmo Consumer vertical (Cosmo Sunshield window films, now in 100+ Indian cities/towns, and Cosmo PPF paint protection films), and grew Zigly's pet-care experience-centre network to over 40 stores as of March 2026, including the acquisition of two veterinary hospitals (Mumbai and Bengaluru). Cosmo First holds six registered patents with eleven more in the pipeline (seven in India, four overseas).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on volume leverage and cost leadership; Cautious on predicting commodity cycles; Aggressive on brand building for consumer verticals; Disciplined on debt and ROCE improvement.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- World's largest thermal lamination film producer and second-largest specialty label film producer globally; among top four global players in BOPP specialty films
- Widest product portfolio under one roof combined with customised innovation, allocation flexibility across job lines, scale, global reach and global warehousing facility
- R&D-led moat: advanced R&D centre in Aurangabad, 30+ researchers including PhDs and post-doctoral professionals, six registered patents with eleven more in pipeline (seven India, four overseas)
- De-commoditising product mix: speciality films accounted for 59% of FY26 sales
- Global distribution reach: exports to 100+ countries, ~44% of sales from exports, office presence in 7 countries

risks.body: Commodity margin volatility (7-8 new BOPP lines in India next 3 years); Delay in US tariff refund processing; Execution risk in scaling consumer brands (marketing burn); Geopolitical impact on West Asia operations.

non_obvious.body: Inventory gains parked in finished goods at port masked some margin benefits in Q4; US tariff refund may require sharing portion with customers who accepted price hikes; Specialty Chemical volume growth (20%) decoupled from revenue growth (10%) due to RM deflation.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Shareholding] Jun-26 pattern: Promoter 40.78%, Institutional 3.93%, Non-Institutional 54.18%, ESOP Trust 1.11% - institutional ownership is notably thin.
- [Tariffs] "US Business Margin expansion post tariff normalization" is listed as a short-term growth driver, implying current US-business margins are tariff-depressed; the deck gives no tariff quantum or timeline.
- [Geopolitics] Raw-material prices rose "post the West Asia conflict", adding Rs 85 Cr to net working capital - the named reason net debt did not fall this quarter.
- [Market context] Addressable markets as stated by the deck: India BOPP ~900K MT pa / Rs 13,000 Cr growing 8-10%; rigid packaging Rs 10,000 Cr growing 10%+; India pet care Rs 25,000 Cr growing 22% pa; India heat-control film ~Rs 1,000 Cr pa growing ~8% with only two producers in India (incl. Cosmo); India PPF ~Rs 500 Cr growing 30% YoY at 1-2% penetration vs ~15% in China.
- [One-offs] Cosmo Plastech's reported Q1 FY27 EBITDA includes a one-time government incentive of Rs 2.4 Cr; excluding it, normalized EBITDA is 7%. FY25 specialty-chemicals EBITDA of Rs 33 Cr is also stated as excluding a one-time incentive.
